question: Should `operator.read` health responses expose runtime-config drift paths and live/disk default model labels for auth/model/provider-related config, with fingerprints and detailed disk errors kept admin-only?
rationale: The code is focused and tested, but the auth-adjacent visibility boundary and per-health disk-read freshness policy are maintainer product/security decisions rather than mechanical correctness issues.

options.title: Approve current diagnostic
options.body: Accept the current `operator.read` drift metadata, admin-only fingerprints/details, and cache-hit disk read as the intended health contract.

options.title: Narrow the visible surface
options.body: Require a follow-up change before merge that makes auth/provider drift admin-only or reduces read-scoped output to a generic restart-required warning.

options.title: Pause diagnostics
options.body: Hold this PR until the companion hot-mode restart policy is resolved so diagnostics and behavior share one maintainer-approved contract.

recommendation.title: Approve current diagnostic
recommendation.body: Accept the current `operator.read` drift metadata, admin-only fingerprints/details, and cache-hit disk read as the intended health contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest history across runtime config snapshots and gateway reload policy, which are the two boundaries this decision crosses.
